newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, PLO leaders in secret summit - source.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, PLO leaders in secret summit - source.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met secretly on Saturday night to try to break a deadlock on a self-rule deal for Hebron, a senior Israeli source said.

It was not immediately clear if they made progress during the meeting which the source said took place at Erez crossing between Israel and the Gaza Strip and was joined by U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross.
The source, who declined to be identified, said they discussed coming to terms on an elusive self-rule deal for Hebron and the further Israeli handover of parts of the West Bank.

"I have no comment," Netanyahu's political adviser Dore Gold, told Reuters when asked about a meeting, first reported by Israel Radio. Senior Palestinian officials said they did not know about a meeting.
Palestinian and Israeli officials had said earlier on Sunday, before news of the meeting leaked out, that several issues still stood in the way of a deal.
Ross has been in the region trying to arrange a summit to hammer out a deal by which Israel would hand over 80 percent of the volatile West Bank town to Palestinian rule.
The handover has been held up for 10 months because of security issues and other concerns.
